ruleset.name: Explicitness Rules
ruleset.description:
Opt-in checks for implicit inputs and implicit outputs (see "Grokking Simplicity", chapter 3). The explicit inputs of a function are its arguments. The explicit output of a function is its return value. All other data that goes into or comes out of a function is implicit, and makes the function an action.
These rules are not part of the default `go` ruleset. The `explicitness` ruleset does not classify receiver reads and writes as implicit inputs or outputs, but it keeps receiver effects as UnknownEffect rather than certifying the method as a calculation. Use `explicitness-strict` to classify receiver reads and writes directly.
Run with: messgo <paths> <format> explicitness

rule.name: ImplicitInput
rule.message: The {0} {1}() has an implicit input: {2}. Pass it in as an argument.
rule.description:
A Go-specific rule (no PHPMD analog). Flags data that goes into a function from a source that is not an argument:
- a read of a package variable that the package changes (a package variable that no code changes is a constant, thus it is not flagged); - a receive from a channel that the function does not declare (<-ch, <-ctx.Done()); - a read from a stream with fmt.Fscan*, io.ReadAll, io.ReadFull, io.ReadAtLeast or io.Copy*; - a standard library call that reads the environment, for example os.Getenv, os.ReadFile, time.Now, time.After, math/rand.Intn, flag.Args, os/exec.Command, net.Dial or net/http.Get; - recover(); - with include-receiver, a read of the receiver or of a receiver field, or a call to a method of the receiver.
Resolved native calls propagate effects to a finite fixed point. Deferred closures have separate summaries, and only invoked callbacks transfer their effects to the caller. Unresolved calls produce UnknownEffect.

property.name: include-receiver
property.description: Also report reads of the receiver of a method.

rule.name: ImplicitOutput
rule.message: The {0} {1}() has an implicit output: {2}. Return it instead.

property.name: include-receiver
property.description: Also report writes through the receiver of a method.

rule.name: UnknownEffect
rule.message: The {0} {1}() has an unknown effect: {2}. Analyze the callee before classifying it as a calculation.
rule.description: Reports calls whose effects cannot be established in the analyzed native subset, including injected callbacks, interface dispatch and opaque external calls. Known actions and unknown operations can coexist. Standard operations are modeled by qualified import path, never by a custom method's name. Receiver effects excluded by policy retain uncertainty. A clean report only establishes a calculation within the documented subset.

property.name: include-receiver
property.description: Analyze receiver effects instead of marking the policy exclusion unknown.

rule.example: func Send(value int, notify func(int)) { notify(value) }
